title: Reducing Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections in ICUs: A Systematic Review of Barriers and Facilitators and Intervention Measures.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite established guidelines, central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) remains a severe ICU complication due to cognitive and resource barriers hindering healthcare worker compliance. A systematic evaluation of these barriers and facilitators is currently lacking but is important for informing targeted implementation strategies for CLABSI prevention. AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement. STUDY DESIGN: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was performed using PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, Wan fang, and CBM databases, up to August 2026. Eligible studies included qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods research on the barriers and facilitators to CLABSI prevention implementation among ICU healthcare workers. Two researchers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Data synthesis and intervention development were guided by the CFIR, with targeted strategies mapped using the CFIR-ERIC (Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change) matching tool. RESULTS: The literature search identified 1,780 records, of which 28 studies were ultimately included. The review identified 28 barriers and facilitators, which were synthesized into four major themes and mapped to 16 CFIR constructs across the catheter-care continuum. The most prominent barriers involved staff knowledge gaps, inconsistent adherence to recommended practices, limited resources, and insufficient leadership support. CFIR-ERIC mapping identified 11 Level 1 expert-endorsed implementation strategies, of which four were represented in the included literature and seven were identified as potential implementation gaps. CONCLUSIONS: CLABSI prevention in ICUs is influenced by multilevel implementation determinants spanning individual, organizational, and practice-related factors. A structured implementation-science approach may help healthcare organizations identify context-specific barriers and prioritize targeted strategies to support more consistent implementation of evidence-based CLABSI prevention practices. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Improving CLABSI prevention may require multilevel strategies that combine targeted education and training, adequate resource allocation, leadership engagement, standardized clinical procedures, and ongoing audit and feedback. These strategies may help strengthen adherence to evidence-based practices, improve quality of care, and enhance patient safety in ICUs.

title: T-cell states in aortic dissection: from molecular immune profiling toward causal and translational validation.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Single-cell RNA sequencing and T-cell receptor profiling reveal substantial T-cell heterogeneity in aortic dissection (AD), but whether these responses contribute to vascular injury or reflect post-onset immune activation remains uncertain. This review evaluates human and experimental evidence by disease stage, tissue compartment, functional validation, T-cell specificity, and intervention timing, distinguishing descriptive profiling from evidence supporting causal and translational inference. DISCUSSION: + Human studies identify Th1/Th17-associated, CD8cytotoxicity-associated, and regulatory T-cell alterations, with stage-related differences in T-cell composition and clonality. Most evidence is cross-sectional and obtained after clinical onset. Antigen specificity, direct aortic-wall cytotoxicity, impaired Treg suppression, and T-cell-mediated aortic-wall injury remain unproven. Single-cell and TCR profiling identify candidate T-cell states and clonotypes for spatial and functional validation, not causal proof. Among candidate pathways, the IL-6-STAT3-IL-17 axis currently has the strongest AD-specific preclinical rationale, but existing interventions are largely non-T-cell-restricted and initiated before or during disease induction. Stronger causal attribution requires convergent human evidence, post-lesion T-cell-restricted perturbation, disease-progression endpoints, and rescue or target-engagement studies. The subacute phase after anatomical and haemodynamic stabilisation may offer a window to study persistent injury-amplifying T-cell responses, whereas early acute and perioperative immunomodulation remains unsupported. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports altered T-cell states after AD onset but does not establish an initiating role. Near-term priorities should be prospective biomarker validation and post-lesion mechanistic studies rather than T-cell-directed immuno-modulation during the early acute and perioperative phases. Clinical translation should await reproducible associations linked to stage-specific causal mechanisms and acceptable safety.

title: High-intensity focused ultrasound as a bridging vascular-modulating therapy for fertility-sparing management of placental site trophoblastic tumor complicated by uterine arteriovenous fistula: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Placental site trophoblastic tumor (PSTT) is a rare gestational trophoblastic neoplasm characterized by local invasiveness and marked vascularity. Surgical management may be associated with substantial bleeding risk and loss of fertility, particularly when complicated by uterine arteriovenous fistula (UAVF). High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) may provide a fertility-preserving adjunctive approach in selected cases. CASE PRESENTATION: A 23-year-old woman presented with persistently plateaued serum human chorionic gonadotropin levels following hysteroscopic management for suspected incomplete abortion. Imaging revealed a deeply invasive hypervascular uterine lesion with UAVF, raising strong suspicion of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. Given her strong desire for fertility preservation and high surgical risk, ultrasound-guided HIFU was performed as an initial vascular-modulating intervention. Subsequent expert pathological review confirmed PSTT. RESULTS: HIFU achieved significant reduction in lesion perfusion and vascular flow, as confirmed by Doppler ultrasound and contrast-enhanced MRI. Although complete tumor ablation was not achieved due to lesion size and deep invasion, subsequent low-dose chemotherapy resulted in complete biochemical remission accompanied by radiologic regression of residual lesions. No major HIFU-related complications were observed, and normal menstrual function resumed during follow-up. CONCLUSION: HIFU is a technically feasible and safe fertility-preserving adjunct for vascular modulation in hypervascular PSTT complicated by UAVF. While HIFU alone may not achieve definitive oncologic control in large or deeply invasive lesions, it can serve as a bridging strategy to reduce tumor perfusion and vascularity, facilitating subsequent systemic therapy in carefully selected patients. This approach demonstrates the potential role of HIFU as a bridging vascular-modulating strategy within multimodal fertility-preserving management.

title: Association between neuromuscular electrical stimulation and intermittent pneumatic compression for the prevention of deep venous thrombosis among neurosurgery patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) considerably affects the incidence and mortality rates in patients undergoing neurosurgery. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) and intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) are frequently used as adjunct treatments to prevent DVT; however, their effects remain unclear. This study was conducted to compare the association of NMES and IPC as two mechanical prophylaxis strategies in neurosurgical patients who were ineligible for pharmacological prophylaxis. METHODS: Postoperative neurosurgical patients were retrospectively enrolled from a single centre between January 2020 and December 2021. These patients were assessed to have a high bleeding risk and received either NMES or IPC as mechanical prophylaxis. Univariable analysis was used to explore the risk factors for DVT, and multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to determine the independent associations between DVT and potential variables after adjusting for confounding factors. RESULTS: p p p p Among 232 patients who underwent neurosurgery, 131 received IPC and 101 received NMES, with no overlap between the two groups. DVT was diagnosed in 62 patients (11 received NMES and 51 received IPC). After controlling for sex, age, operation duration and length of hospital stay, NMES use was associated with a lower incidence of DVT (OR = 0.268, 95% CI = 0.125-0.576, = .001). Moreover, men were less likely to have DVT than women (OR = 0.469, 95% CI = 0.242-0.910, = .025), older age was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 3.419, 95% CI = 1.594-7.334, = .002), and a longer operation duration was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 2.180, 95% CI = 1.042-4.560, = .039). CONCLUSION: This study found an association between NMES and reduced odds of DVT compared with IPC in neurosurgery patients. Although NMES may be more widely adopted in neurosurgery to decrease the incidence of DVT, further evidence is required to determine its effectiveness in clinical practice.

title: Clinical outcomes of total endovascular aortic arch repair by in situ microneedle fenestration using the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique.
abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the outcomes of total endovascular aortic arch repair (TEAAR) via in situ micro-needle fenestration (ISMNF) with the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, the data of consecutive patients who underwent TEAAR via ISMNF with triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique between August 2022 and April 2025 were analyzed. Three 6-Fr, 90-cm sheaths were placed into ascending aorta without removing the dilator and super-stiff guidewires during main stent-graft deployment. This configuration creates a gutter between the stent-graft and aortic wall to maintain perfusion to supra-aortic branches. Operative details, technical success, 30-day and midterm outcomes, and adverse events were recorded. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate freedom from all-cause death and reintervention. RESULTS: Overall, 36 patients were included. The technical success rate was 94.4% (34/36). Endovascular reconstruction of cervical branches was successfully performed in all cases. The 30-day mortality was 2.8%. The median follow-up period was 19 months (range, 1-32 months). The all-cause death rate was 11.1% (4/36), with no cases of any aorta-related death. The prevalence of endoleaks during follow-up was 13.9% (5/36). The overall stroke rate was 8.3% (3/36). The 1- and 2-year survival rates were 97.3% ± 2.7% and 85.8% ± 8.1%, respectively. The cumulative rate of freedom from reintervention at 1 and 2 years was 87.5% ± 5.9% and 83.2% ± 7.0%, respectively. CONCLUSION: TEAAR via ISMNF with the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique was performed with a 94% technical success rate and stroke risk similar to open surgery.

title: Characteristics of treatment responses to physical exercise and diet in diabetic peripheral artery disease patients: a systematic review.
abstract: PURPOSE: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects walking performance and increases risk of amputation. Diabetes mellitus (DM) not only contributes to disease progression but may also affect treatment effects. Though physical exercise is crucial in PAD management and diet optimization may reduce risk of atherosclerosis, their effects and variations in diabetic PAD patients remain unclear. The present systematic review aims to summarize features of treatment response to physical exercise and diet management in diabetic PAD patients, and provide crucial information on optimization of PAD management of these patients in clinical practice. METHODS: A systematic review was performed on human studies investigating effects of physical exercise and diet on development and improvement of diabetic PAD patients by searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and CINAHL. The review was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analysis (PRISMA). The certainty level of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE). RESULTS: A total of 18 studies were included, 15 of which evaluated effects of exercise on diabetic PAD, and three evaluated correlation between diet and diabetic PAD. Supervised exercise therapy (SET) and home-based exercise were able to improve ankle-brachial index (ABI) and blood flow velocity in diabetic PAD. In contrast, walking performance such as the six minute walk distance (6MWD), maximal walking time and distance, peak walking time (PWT) and claudication onset time (COT) were not significantly improved or presented conflicting results. Administration of multiple exercises or alternative interventions such as shock wave therapy or low-frequency pulsed electromagnetic field therapy (LFPMT) may enhance improvement of ABI. Adherence to Mediterranean diet was associated with blood flow and intermittent claudication, as well as risk of development of PAD. GRADE analysis revealed very low to moderate grade evidence for findings on ABI, flow velocity and functions, mainly due to study types, number of studies available, small sample size, moderate risk of bias and conflicting results. Similarly, low grade evidence was also revealed for effects and association of diet on risk of PAD due to study type and number of studies available. CONCLUSION: Diabetic PAD patients may present reduced treatment response to physical exercise in walking performance and other functions, which may be improved by combination of multiple physical exercises or alternative interventions with or without combination of exercise. Mediterranean diet may be associated with beneficial effects, which requires further investigations. These findings were of very low to moderate level of certainty, and therefore, further validation is warranted in the future.

title: Dissecting cell-type-specific genetic associations between colorectal cancer liability and thrombotic risk in peripheral blood immune cells.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major complication of colorectal cancer (CRC), but whether CRC-associated thrombotic susceptibility includes cell-specific inherited regulatory components in peripheral blood remains unclear. To investigate associations between CRC genetic liability and VTE-related outcomes within peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) regulatory contexts. We integrated CRC GWAS, FinnGen VTE-related outcomes, and TenK10K PBMC single-cell eQTL data across 28 immune cell types using cell-stratified Mendelian randomization (csMR). Prioritized signals were further examined in single-cell RNA-seq datasets and bulk transcriptomes. Conventional MR showed no clear evidence that CRC liability increased VTE, DVT, or PE risk, and LD Score regression detected no significant genome-wide genetic correlation. In contrast, csMR identified nominal, cell-context-dependent associations. B intermediate cells were prioritized across VTE (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.03-1.32), DVT (OR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.08-1.57), and PE (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.07-1.49), while CD14 + monocytes and CD4 + central memory T cells received additional support from downstream single-cell analyses. Gene-level analyses prioritized LAMA5, LIMA1, and TRIM28 in these respective cell contexts. In bulk blood, RPS21 showed consistent disease-associated expression patterns and discriminated VTE patients from healthy controls in an external dataset (AUC, 0.865; 95% CI, 0.800-0.923). These findings suggest that genetic overlap between CRC liability and thrombotic phenotypes may be localized to selected PBMC regulatory contexts rather than broadly detectable genome-wide. Among the prioritized signals, B intermediate cells showed the most consistent csMR associations across VTE, DVT, and PE. The cell-gene pairs, together with RPS21, warrant independent genetic, functional, and prospective validation as candidates for studying peripheral immune regulation and blood-based markers of CRC-associated thrombosis.

title: Association of modified cardiovascular health with long-term all-cause mortality among adults with Ankle-Brachial Index-defined peripheral artery disease: a NHANES 1999-2004 cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether an integrated cardiovascular health profile is associated with long-term mortality among adults with objectively defined peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains insufficiently characterized in nationally representative cohorts. METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2004 participants aged ≥40 years with Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) measurements and linked mortality follow-up through December 31, 2019. PAD was defined as a minimum ABI ≤0.90. Modified cardiovascular health (mCVH; range 0-12) was constructed from smoking, Body Mass Index, physical activity, blood pressure, total cholesterol, and glycemic status. Corrected six-year Mobile Examination Center weights and complex survey design variables were used. Weighted Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for all-cause mortality using sequential adjustment for demographic factors, socioeconomic factors, survey cycle, and minimum ABI. Additional analyses evaluated non-PAD participants and cardiovascular mortality. RESULTS: The primary PAD cohort included 554 adults, among whom 428 deaths occurred during a median follow-up of 123.5 months. PAD participants had a higher absolute all-cause mortality burden than non-PAD participants. Each 1-point higher mCVH score was associated with lower all-cause mortality in Model 1 (HR 0.888, 95% CI 0.842-0.937; P<0.001), Model 2 (HR 0.922, 95% CI 0.870-0.977; P=0.006), and Model 3 (HR 0.926, 95% CI 0.874-0.982; P=0.010). Among non-PAD participants, higher mCVH was also associated with lower all-cause mortality, and the mCVH × PAD status interaction was not statistically significant (P=0.122). In sensitivity analysis, higher mCVH was also associated with lower cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.863, 95% CI 0.786-0.948; P=0.002). Component-level analyses suggested that smoking was the most robust individual component. CONCLUSIONS: Among U.S. adults with ABI-defined PAD, higher baseline mCVH was associated with lower long-term all-cause mortality. These findings support the prognostic relevance of integrated cardiovascular health profiling after objective PAD identification, while highlighting smoking as the most consistent individual component.

title: Functional Vulnerability and Long-Term Mortality in Adults With Ankle-Brachial Index-Defined Peripheral Artery Disease: A NHANES Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Functional limitations are common in peripheral artery disease (PAD), but the association of a brief self-reported functional-burden measure with objectively defined PAD and long-term mortality remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2004 participants aged >=40 years with ankle-brachial index (ABI), physical functioning, and linked mortality data. PAD was defined as minimum ABI <=0.90. A NHANES-derived functional vulnerability index (NFVI; range 0-4) was constructed from difficulty walking a quarter mile, walking up ten steps, stooping/crouching/kneeling, and standing for long periods. NFVI was intended as a brief functional-burden measure rather than a diagnostic frailty instrument. Survey-weighted models evaluated PAD status, NFVI, and mortality, with validated modified cardiovascular health (mCVH) used for additional adjustment. RESULTS: The PAD NFVI cohort included 462 participants and 375 deaths. PAD was associated with high NFVI after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and mCVH (OR 1.748, 95% CI 1.218-2.510; P=0.005). In PAD participants, each 1-point higher NFVI was associated with all-cause mortality after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and minimum ABI (HR 1.095, 95% CI 1.017-1.179; P=0.017). After additional mCVH adjustment, the continuous association was attenuated (HR 1.075, 95% CI 0.993-1.165; P=0.075), whereas high NFVI remained associated with mortality (HR 1.346, 95% CI 1.026-1.767; P=0.032). Complete-case selection was substantial (462/647 PAD participants), with marked differences between included and excluded participants, particularly in age, potentially limiting generalizability. CONCLUSIONS: Functional vulnerability was more common among adults with ABI-defined PAD and was associated with long-term all-cause mortality. These findings demonstrate an epidemiologic association rather than the clinical utility, validation, or incremental prognostic value of NFVI and do not establish a clinically meaningful NFVI mortality threshold. Prospective PAD-specific validation and comparison with established frailty measures are required before clinical use.

title: Effects of Endovascular Repair Timing on the Outcomes of Type B Aortic Dissection in an Asian Multicenter Cohort.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study assessed thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) timing and its impact on outcomes in type B aortic dissection (TBAD). METHOD: This multicenter retrospective study included 247 patients who underwent TEVAR for TBAD between 2011 and 2018, using data from the Chang Gung Research Database. Primary outcomes were in-hospital and postdischarge mortality. RESULTS: The study included 47, 122, and 78 patients with hyperacute (<1 day), acute/subacute (1-90 days), and chronic (>90 days) TBAD, respectively. Chronic TBAD had more aortic expansion before TEVAR (0% vs 6.6% vs 17.6%; P = 0.001). In-hospital mortality was highest in hyperacute TBAD (17%) and lowest in chronic TBAD (6.4%; adjusted P for trend = 0.036); conversely, long-term mortality was highest in chronic TBAD (12.3%) and lowest in hyperacute TBAD (0%; adjusted P for trend = 0.017). A restricted cubic spline model showed that delayed intervention beyond 90 days is associated with increasing long-term mortality risk. Among secondary outcomes, delayed TEVAR was associated with more aortic, cardiovascular, infection-related deaths, and residual aneurysms (adjusted P for trend= 0.039, 0.012, 0.048, and 0.006, respectively). CONCLUSIONS: TEVAR may lead to unfavorable outcomes in hyperacute and chronic TBAD. Delayed TEVAR in chronic TBAD is associated with adverse aortic remodeling and rising long-term mortality. TEVAR before the chronic phase could be considered to improve short- and long-term outcomes.

title: Ultrasound-guided selective nerve block promotes perioperative vascular remodeling and early maturation of radiocephalic arteriovenous fistulas.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for maintenance hemodialysis, but its successful maturation depends on adequate perioperative vascular remodeling. We evaluated whether ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB) promotes vascular remodeling and improves AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation. METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis based on a prospectively-maintained single-center vascular-access clinical follow-up database. We included 163 patients with stage 5 chronic kidney disease undergoing primary radiocephalic AVF creation between January 2023 and January 2024. Patients received ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB, n=72) or local infiltration anesthesia (LA, n=91). Perioperative changes in radial artery and cephalic vein diameters were evaluated, postoperative brachial artery blood flow was recorded, and AVF maturation was assessed at 1, 2, and 3 months. Linear mixed-effects models and multivariable logistic regression were used for analysis. RESULTS: Compared with LA, SNB significantly increased radial artery and cephalic vein diameters after anesthesia, whereas both vessels constricted in the LA group (both P<0.001). Linear mixed-effects analysis demonstrated significant time effects and group-by-time interactions for both vessels, while a significant group effect was observed only for the cephalic vein (all P<0.001). Postoperative brachial artery blood flow was significantly greater in the SNB group (P<0.001). The 2-month AVF maturation rate was significantly higher in the SNB group than in the LA group (60% vs. 35%, P=0.002), whereas no between-group differences were observed at 1 or 3 months. Younger age, larger preoperative radial artery diameter, and SNB were independent predictors of AVF maturation. CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided selective nerve block promotes perioperative vascular remodeling, increases postoperative blood flow, and independently facilitates early AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation. These findings support SNB as a promising perioperative strategy to optimize vascular access outcomes in patients undergoing AVF creation.

We evaluated whether ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB) promotes vascular remodeling and improves AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation. METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis based on a prospectively-maintained single-center vascular-access clinical follow-up database.

title: Association of circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography with preoperative rupture in type A aortic dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography (CTA) and preoperative rupture in patients with type A aortic dissection (TAAD). METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 597 consecutive patients diagnosed with TAAD at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Patients were classified into circumferential dissection (n = 130) and non-circumferential dissection (n = 467) groups based on preoperative CTA. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging characteristics were compared between groups. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to examine factors independently associated with preoperative rupture, and between-group differences in preoperative rupture were compared. RESULTS: Circumferential dissection was strongly associated with DeBakey type I dissection, supra-aortic branch involvement, and greater false-lumen expansion with true-lumen compression. Preoperative rupture occurred more frequently in patients with circumferential dissection than in those without (33.8% vs 7.1%, P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that circumferential dissection was independently associated with preoperative rupture ascertained by bedside echocardiography following the admission CTA after adjustment for demographic, laboratory, and imaging factors (OR = 5.24, 95% CI: 1.86-14.76, P = 0.002). CONCLUSION: Circumferential dissection on CTA is independently associated with preoperative rupture and may support timely surgical decision-making in TAAD.

title: Cross-elbow stent placement for refractory arteriovenous fistula stenosis and chronic total occlusion in hemodialysis patients: a single-center retrospective cohort of 42 cases.
abstract: Cross-elbow stent placement in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) has been avoided due to risks of fracture, kinking, deformation, migration, and infection. However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage. Consecutive adult hemodialysis patients who received cross-elbow stents for clinically significant AVF stenosis or CTO (September 2021 - March 2026) at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Primary outcomes were target lesion primary patency (TLPP), access circuit primary patency (ACPP), access circuit secondary patency, and access circuit assisted primary patency, estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Technical and clinical success and complications were recorded. Forty-two patients were included; 45.2% had CTO and 57.1% had prior PTA. Eluvia-based stents were used in 83.3%. Technical and clinical success were both 100%. Mean access flow increased from 407 ± 267 to 839 ± 188 mL/min. TLPP at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months was 90.1%, 84.4%, 76.9%, and 76.9%, respectively. No stent fracture, migration, kinking, or infection occurred. Cross-elbow stenting was technically feasible and provided favorable short- to mid-term patency without device-related complications, supporting its use as a salvage option for selected refractory AVF lesions and CTOs.

title: Development and Clinical Validation of a Stroke Risk Decision System for Patients With Carotid Artery Plaque Based on AI-Powered Handheld Ultrasound and Laboratory Markers.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and validate a fusion model combining portable artificial intelligence (AI) ultrasound imaging with multidimensional laboratory data to stratify risk and support decision-making in patients with carotid plaque-related anterior circulation stroke, and to assess its predictive performance and clinical utility. METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 639 patients with carotid plaque via AI-powered ultrasound at community health centers. Anterior circulation stroke (ACS)/transient ischemic attack (TIA) patients were excluded. All participants completed the 180-day follow-up. The primary outcome was new-onset anterior circulation stroke or TIA, defined as focal neurological deficit > 24 h with CT/MRI-confirmed infarction, or transient (< 24 h) deficit without evidence of acute infarction on neuroimaging. Outcomes were adjudicated by two neurologists (attending or above), with a third for disagreements. Participants were classified into ACS group (n = 140) and non-ACS group (n = 499). Ultrasound features of carotid plaques and clinical laboratory data were compared between the two groups. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with ACS, and a nomogram was constructed based on the regression model. Internal validation was conducted using the bootstrap method. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination (C-index and area under the curve [AUC]), calibration (calibration curves), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis [DCA] and clinical impact curves [CIC]). RESULTS: (1) Significant differences were observed between the two groups in history of hypertension, smoking, hyperlipidemia, stroke, and myocardial infarction (MI), as well as plasma triglyceride (TG), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels, carotid plaque thickness, plaque area, plaque echogenicity percentage, degree of carotid stenosis, plaque continuity score, and plaque mutability score (p < 0.05). No significant differences were found in sex, history of diabetes, total cholesterol (TC), plaque location, or plaque fibrous cap continuity analysis score (p > 0.05) (2) Multivariable logistic regression identified history of stroke, history of myocardial infarction, plaque thickness, LDL, and HDL as independent predictors of stroke. A nomogram based on these factors demonstrated good discrimination (C-index/AUC = 0.884), with a sensitivity of 84.29% and specificity of 72.55%, along with excellent calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test p = 0.250). Decision curve analysis showed superior net benefit across a range of risk thresholds compared with the null model, supporting a multi-threshold stratified intervention strategy. Notably, when the predicted risk exceeded 75%, the model's predictions closely aligned with observed outcomes. CONCLUSION: The stroke risk decision system developed using AI-powered handheld ultrasound and laboratory indicators demonstrates clinical applicability for early prediction of anterior circulation ischemic stroke and is particularly suitable for early screening and risk stratification of high-risk stroke populations in resource-limited settings.

title: Trends in incident hemodialysis access and mortality in China: results from China Renal Data System 2000-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUNDS: Large‑scale multicenter data on vascular access among Chinese incident hemodialysis (HD) patients are limited. We explored temporal trends of initial vascular access and its relationship with all‑cause mortality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted using the China Renal Data System, enrolling incident HD patients from January 2000 to April 2024. Vascular access trends and distribution at HD initiation were analyzed. RESULTS: 16,717 patients were enrolled (mean age 55.62 ± 10.93 years; 61.54% male; mean follow‑up 64.41 months). At HD initiation, 29.17% of patients used arteriovenous fistula/graft (AVF/AVG), while 70.83% used central venous catheter (CVC), comprising 60.78% with a maturing AVF/AVG and 10.06% with CVC alone. AVF/AVG use increased from 26.24% in 2015 to 35.77% in 2024, while CVC-only use decreased from 16.16% to 8.27%. Mortality rates per 100 person-years were 4.15 (95% confidence interval [CI] 3.93 - 4.38), 7.24 (95% CI 7.00 - 7.49), and 15.08 (95% CI 14.07 - 16.15) in the AVF/AVG, CVC with maturing AVF/AVG, and CVC-only groups, respectively. In the adjusted Cox model, patients using CVC with a maturing AVF/AVG or CVC alone exhibited 36% and 91% higher all-cause mortality risks, respectively, compared with those using AVF/AVG. CONCLUSIONS: Over the 25-year period, initial vascular access among Chinese incident HD patients gradually shifted from CVC to AVF/AVG, reflecting ongoing and considerable improvements in vascular access practice in China. CVC use at HD initiation was associated with higher all-cause mortality compared with AVF/AVG. These findings support early AVF/AVG creation in end-stage kidney disease patients to avoid CVC use at HD initiation.

title: Silymarin attenuates neuroinflammation after subarachnoid hemorrhage by inducing M2 microglial polarization via activation of the JAK1/STAT6 signaling pathway.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Neuroinflammation represents a key pathological process in early brain injury (EBI) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and contributes significantly to poor outcomes. Silymarin, known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified. An in vivo endovascular perforation model and an in vitro hemoglobin-stimulated model were used to investigate the pharmacological effects of silymarin in SAH. Neurological function was assessed using SAH scores and neurobehavioral scores. Neuronal apoptosis was evaluated by TUNEL staining. Neuroinflammation was measured by ELISA or qPCR, and microglial polarization status was determined by assessing CD86 and CD206 expression via Western blotting (WB) or immunofluorescence (IF) staining. Ruxolitinib and AS1517499 were applied to block the JAK1/STAT6 pathway. Silymarin attenuated early brain injury (EBI) after SAH, as indicated by improved neurological scores, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and lower brain water content. In vivo, silymarin treatment was associated with JAK1/STAT6 activation, elevated M2 markers, and decreased pro‑inflammatory cytokines. In vitro, silymarin activated the JAK1/STAT6 pathway, promoted M2 microglial polarization, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production. In addition, pharmacological blockade of JAK1/STAT6 reversed silymarin's protective effects, confirming a causal role of this pathway in the cellular context. Our in vitro data demonstrate that silymarin directly stimulates JAK1/STAT6 to drive M2 polarization and anti‑inflammatory responses. In vivo, we observed a correlation between pathway activation and neuroprotective benefits. Together, these findings provide a rationale for further exploring silymarin‑based therapies in SAH. title: Long-term outcome of stenting for the iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral arterio-venous graft; a case series.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the possible etiology and evaluate the technical and clinical outcomes of using bare metal stents for the treatment of central venous stenosis (CVS) in the lower extremity with ipsilateral hemodialysis access. METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis of a small case series was conducted in hemodialysis patients with lower extremity arteriovenous grafts (AVG) who were treated with bare metal stents (BMS) for symptomatic iliac vein stenosis between April 2016 and June 2021. Patients' demographic data, technical details, adverse events, clinical outcomes, and imaging data were recorded. RESULTS: The study cohort comprised seven females and four males, with a mean age of 58.8 ± 13.4 years. Preoperative lower limb venography was performed in nine patients scheduled for AVG creation. With the exception of one case demonstrating left iliac vein compression, the iliac veins were patent in all other patients. Symptoms of lower limb swelling developed at a mean interval of 9.40 ± 5.83 months (range: 3-20 months) following AVG placement. Eight cases had a concomitant history of temporary ipsilateral femoral vein catheterization. Lesion characteristics included nine stenotic lesions and two occlusive lesions. All patients were treated with SMART Control stents (Cordis Corp, USA). The technical success rate was 100%, and symptomatic relief was achieved in all cases. Over a mean follow-up period of 47.8 ± 31.7 months (range: 10-123 months), the target lesion primary patency was 100% (one-side confidence interval [CI] = 0.74,1). CONCLUSIONS: Using BMS is a safe and effective method to treat iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral AVG.

title: Bilateral peripheral CT venography for evaluating central venous lesions in dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas: feasibility, safety, and radiation dose in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Central venous stenosis and occlusion are major causes of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction in hemodialysis patients. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, radiation exposure, and anatomical findings of bilateral peripheral CT venography for central venous assessment in patients with dysfunctional AVFs. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 46 consecutive hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs who underwent bilateral peripheral CT venography between August 2023 and June 2025. Technical success, procedure-related adverse events, radiation dose parameters, central venous lesion characteristics, and agreement with available comparative imaging modalities were analyzed. Comparative imaging findings from puncture-based angiography and/or duplex ultrasonography were assessed descriptively. RESULTS: All 46 examinations were technically successful (100%), with a mean procedure duration of 4 minutes (range, 3-5 minutes). Minor adverse events included one patient of contrast extravasation (2.2%) and 3 of mild allergic reactions (6.5%); no severe procedure-related complications were documented. The mean CTDIvol and DLP were 11.87 mGy and 784.15 mGy·cm, respectively. Central venous abnormalities were identified in 44 patients (95.7%), including stenosis in 31 (67.4%), occlusion in 11 (23.9%), and aneurysmal changes in 2 (4.3%). Comparative imaging was available in 38 patients, and CT venography showed agreement with available findings in 37 cases (97.4%). This agreement was interpreted as descriptive concordance rather than formal diagnostic accuracy. CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral peripheral CT venography demonstrated high technical feasibility, acceptable safety, and effective visualization of central venous abnormalities in hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs. Further prospective studies are needed to validate its diagnostic performance and clinical impact. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This technique enables efficient, noninvasive assessment of central venous pathology with minimal risk, supporting its potential as a practical alternative to conventional imaging in hemodialysis patients.

title: Analysis of risk factors and construction of a prediction model for postoperative deep vein thrombosis in patients with periarticular knee fractures.
abstract: The present study aimed to identify risk factors for postoperative deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in patients with periarticular knee fractures. A prediction model was constructed for the early identification of high-risk patients. Data from 319 patients at who underwent surgery at the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University (Luzhou, China) between January 2020 and December 2022 were analyzed. Based on ultrasound results, patients were divided into a DVT group (n=83) and a non-DVT group (n=236). Logistic regression was employed to identify independent risk factors. Subsequently, a nomogram model was established, which was validated via receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). The DVT rate was 26.0%. Old age (OR, 1.0228), high American Society of Anesthesiologists grade (OR, 2.2764), greater blood loss (OR, 1.0015), blood transfusion (OR, 2.7917) and high D-dimer levels (OR, 1.0251) were identified as independent risk factors (P<0.05), while living in cities, high hemoglobin, high prealbumin, high Barthel index and high Braden scores served as protective factors (P<0.05). The model yielded an area under the curve value of 0.837. Additionally, the calibration curve showed high accuracy, and DCA validated the favorable clinical applicability of this predictive model. In conclusion, the model performs well in helping doctors to identify high-risk patients and optimize individualized therapeutic strategies.

title: Management of Brachial Plexus Neurogenic Tumors: A Retrospective Study of 25 Cases.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: To investigate the clinical characteristics of cervical brachial plexus neurogenic tumors and enhance the diagnostic and therapeutic management of this condition. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 25 patients diagnosed with brachial plexus neurogenic tumors who were treated at a tertiary teaching hospital between January 2019 and December 2024. Clinical manifestations, treatment strategies, and follow-up outcomes were systematically summarized. RESULTS: A total of 25 patients were included, treated across multiple departments: otorhinolaryngology-head and neck surgery, neurosurgery, orthopedics, thyroid surgery, and vascular surgery. There were 13 male and 12 female patients, aged 16-76 y, with a disease duration ranging from 1 wk to 2 y, defined as the interval from symptom onset to initial clinical evaluation. The primary presenting symptom was a neck root mass in 21 patients, among whom seven experienced ipsilateral upper limb numbness, soreness, or electric shock-like pain upon palpation and four reported sensory disturbances in the upper extremity or shoulder-back pain. All patients underwent cervical contrast-enhanced computed tomography, and 18 additionally received 3.0 T magnetic resonance imaging. Preoperative ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration cytology was performed in all cases, revealing spindle cell tumors with morphological features suggestive of schwannoma. Of the 25 patients, 23 underwent surgical resection, while two with small tumors (<2 cm), no neurological symptoms, and cytologically benign findings opted for conservative management with close observation. Surgical approaches included the anterior supraclavicular approach, the posterior cervical paravertebral approach, and clavicle-splitting (transclavicular) approach. Postoperative pathological examination confirmed benign schwannoma in 22 cases and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor in one case. Follow-up duration ranged from 12 to 60 mo. Transient postoperative neurological dysfunction occurred in five patients, manifesting as limited shoulder abduction, reduced wrist extensor strength, or limb numbness; all deficits resolved within 6 mo following structured rehabilitation programs. CONCLUSIONS: Brachial plexus neurogenic tumors commonly present as a mass in the neck root, with a subset of cases accompanied by neurological symptoms. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging are valuable modalities for tumor localization and qualitative characterization. Preoperative fine needle aspiration cytology enables a preliminary assessment of tumor histology. The selection of an appropriate surgical approach should be guided by tumor location and anatomical involvement. Intralesional enucleation is a key strategy for preserving neurological function, and when combined with microsurgical techniques and intraoperative nerve monitoring, even transient postoperative neurological deficits can be effectively managed through structured rehabilitation programs.

title: Association between admission D-dimer levels and post-stroke epilepsy risk: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-stroke epilepsy (PSE) is a severe complication following acute ischemic stroke (AIS), yet early identification of patients at high risk remains challenging. This study evaluated the association between baseline D-dimer levels and incident PSE within one year after AIS. METHODS: 2 In this secondary analysis of a multicenter retrospective cohort, 21,459 patients with first-ever AIS were included. D-dimer was modeled as a log-transformed continuous variable. Multivariable logistic regression with progressive adjustment, restricted cubic spline analysis, and sensitivity analyses were performed. Internal validation was conducted using bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: The median baseline D-dimer level was 0.92 mg/L (IQR 0.65-1.49). PSE occurred in 936 patients (4.36%). After full adjustment, each doubling of D-dimer was associated with a 3.3-fold increase in PSE odds (OR 3.33, 95% CI 2.94-3.78). The association remained consistent in sensitivity analyses excluding patients with deep vein thrombosis (OR 3.86, 95% CI 3.37-4.43), atrial fibrillation (OR 3.50, 95% CI 3.04-4.04), or extreme D-dimer values (OR 3.41, 95% CI 2.99-3.91). A non-linear relationship was observed, with PSE risk rising more steeply at higher D-dimer levels. The C-statistic for the fully adjusted model was 0.968. CONCLUSION: Elevated baseline D-dimer levels were independently associated with an increased risk of PSE within one year after AIS. As a routinely available biomarker, D-dimer may inform risk assessment in acute stroke units; however, external validation in independent cohorts with prospective PSE ascertainment is required before clinical implementation.

title: High BMI-attributable burden of eight diseases relevant to the CKM framework in China: GBD 2023 estimates and projections to 2050.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a recently defined clinical entity integrating metabolic risk factors, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease. Elevated body mass index (BMI) is a major modifiable risk factor for CKM syndrome, yet comprehensive long-term analyses of the high BMI-attributable burden in China remain scarce. METHODS: Using data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 study, we assessed the burden of eight selected CKM-related diseases attributable to high BMI (atrial fibrillation and flutter [AFF], chronic kidney disease due to hypertension [CKD-HTN] or diabetes mellitus type 2 [CKD-T2DM], diabetes mellitus type 2 [T2DM], hypertensive heart disease [HHD], ischemic heart disease [IHD], lower extremity peripheral arterial disease [LEPAD], and stroke) in China from 1990 to 2023. The primary outcomes were absolute deaths and DALYs and their age-standardized rates (ASRs) per 100,000 population. Joinpoint regression and ARIMA models were applied to analyze and project temporal trends in ASRs, age-period-cohort analysis was conducted using age-specific rates, and decomposition analysis quantified the contributions of population growth, population aging, and epidemiological change to changes in absolute deaths and DALYs. RESULTS: From 1990 to 2023, absolute deaths and DALYs for all eight selected diseases relevant to the CKM framework increased. IHD had the highest burden in 2023 (114,980 deaths; 2,923,595 DALYs), whereas AFF showed the greatest relative increase (11.4-fold). Descriptively, men generally had higher point estimates of death and DALY counts, ASMRs, and ASDRs for CKD-T2DM, CKD-HTN, IHD, and HHD, whereas women had higher corresponding estimates for AFF. Joinpoint regression identified sustained increases in AFF, IHD, T2DM, and LEPAD, with several inflection points around 2005. APC analysis showed pronounced age-related gradients and variations in period and cohort rate ratios. Decomposition analysis indicated that population aging was the predominant contributor to increasing mortality for most outcomes, while epidemiological change had heterogeneous effects and partially offset increases in CKD-T2DM and HHD. Model-based projections suggested heterogeneous future trajectories: increasing mortality and DALY rates for AFF, IHD, and LEPAD; increasing DALYs but slightly declining mortality for T2DM; broadly stable or slightly declining rates for stroke, CKD-T2DM, and CKD-HTN; and declining point estimates for HHD, although with substantial long-term uncertainty. CONCLUSION: High BMI-attributable stage 2-4 CKM burden has risen sharply in China and will continue to increase, driven mainly by worsening epidemiological risks. AFF, IHD, and LEPAD show the fastest growth. Men had higher age-standardized mortality and DALY rates for several selected diseases. Early-life obesity prevention and sex-tailored interventions are urgently needed.

title: Hemodynamic Insights Into an Accessory Splenic Artery Aneurysm Arising From the Superior Mesenteric Artery.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Splenic artery variations involve anomalies in origin, course, and branching. Notably, the accessory splenic artery (ASA) is a rare independent, ectopic aberrant duplication outside the celiac trunk, making its comprehension crucial for safety during endovascular interventions. CASE SUMMARY: This case report describes a 34-year-old woman with a rare splenic artery duplication, consisting of a primary splenic artery normally originating from the celiac trunk and an ASA arising from the superior mesenteric artery that harbored a distal saccular aneurysm. DISCUSSION: An ASA originating from the superior mesenteric artery and associated with aneurysm formation is an extremely rare anatomical variation. Hemodynamic evaluations based on computational fluid dynamics simulation indicated that the unique vascular configuration of this aberrant artery may predispose the aneurysm to an elevated risk of rupture. TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This type of accessory splenic artery originating from the superior mesenteric artery is reported here for the first time.

title: Retrograde Collateral Crossing Through Riolan's Arcade With Femoral Antegrade Reconstruction After Traction During Upper-Extremity Externalization.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Flush superior mesenteric artery (SMA) occlusion without a discernible stump remains one of the most challenging scenarios in the endovascular treatment of chronic mesenteric ischemia. CASE SUMMARY: A 59-year-old woman presented with chronic mesenteric ischemia. Computed tomographic angiography demonstrated flush SMA occlusion with collateral perfusion through Riolan's arcade. Antegrade crossing failed because the SMA ostium could not be selectively engaged. Retrograde collateral crossing through Riolan's arcade was successfully achieved. Although upper-extremity externalization was technically successful, progressive abdominal pain developed during sustained traction, raising concern for excessive mesenteric tension and potential collateral vessel injury. The reconstruction strategy was therefore converted to a femoral antegrade approach. Successful SMA revascularization was achieved. Symptoms resolved, and follow-up computed tomographic angiography confirmed sustained SMA patency. DISCUSSION: This case highlights a strategy of retrograde collateral crossing followed by femoral antegrade reconstruction for flush SMA occlusion. Conversion to femoral reconstruction may reduce collateral traction while facilitating definitive endovascular treatment. TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: In complex SMA chronic total occlusion, retrograde collateral crossing through Riolan's arcade can facilitate lesion traversal, whereas femoral antegrade reconstruction may offer a lower-traction and more controlled pathway for definitive mesenteric revascularization.

title: Incidence, Risk Factors, and Outcomes of Early Post-Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt Hyperbilirubinemia.
abstract: PURPOSE: To determine the incidence, risk factors, and outcomes of early post-transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) hyperbilirubinemia in cirrhotic patients. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 1,404 cirrhotic patients who underwent TIPS were analyzed. Patients with early post-TIPS hyperbilirubinemia (total bilirubin [TB] ≥ 5 mg/dL within 1 week after TIPS; primary predictor) were classified as Group A, and those without it were classified as Group B. Threshold effect analysis was used to identify the optimal cutoff for the change in TB (exploratory parameter), followed by Fine-Gray modeling. RESULTS: Early post-TIPS hyperbilirubinemia occurred in 67 patients (4.8%). The cumulative incidence of mortality was higher in Group A than in Group B at 1 year (37.3% vs 7.7%), 3 years (49.7% vs 19.8%), and 5 years (49.7% vs 30.3%; P < .001). Multivariate analysis identified early post-TIPS hyperbilirubinemia (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 3.03; P < .001), age (sHR, 1.05; P < .001), albumin level (sHR, 0.96; P < .001), model for end-stage liver disease score (sHR, 1.05; P = .005), and hepatocellular carcinoma (sHR, 1.77; P < .001) as independent predictors of mortality. Change in TB was independently associated with mortality whether analyzed as a continuous variable (sHR, 1.19; P < .001) or dichotomized at 2.98 mg/dL (sHR, 2.64; P < .001). Rounding the cutoff to 3 mg/dL did not materially alter the association (sHR, 2.58; P < .001). CONCLUSION: TB ≥ 5 mg/dL within the first week after TIPS, or ΔTB ≥ 2.98mg/dL (∼3 mg/dL) was independently associated with mortality.

title: Deep learning versus radiologists for acute aortic dissection on CT: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
abstract: Acute aortic dissection (AAD) is a time-sensitive cardiovascular emergency in which delayed recognition remains associated with poor early outcomes, and deep learning (DL) applied to computed tomography (CT) is increasingly proposed for triage support. We synthesized DL detection accuracy on CT, compared DL with radiologists head-to-head, and secondarily pooled CT segmentation accuracy. This Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-compliant review searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science through February 18, 2026. Detection studies were pooled with bivariate random-effects models; head-to-head comparisons were synthesized with contrast-based network meta-analysis; segmentation Sørensen-Dice coefficients were analyzed with three-level random-effects models. Twenty-three studies were included. For non-contrast CT detection (10 studies; 18 cohorts; 54 algorithm-cohort datasets), pooled sensitivity was 0.91 (95 % confidence interval [CI], 0.87-0.94) and specificity 0.90 (95 % CI, 0.85-0.94). In direct comparisons (5 studies; 11 comparisons), radiologist-to-DL relative sensitivity was 0.72 (95 % CI, 0.57-0.91) and relative specificity 0.88 (95 % CI, 0.83-0.93). For the secondary segmentation synthesis (16 studies; 88 datasets), pooled Dice was 0.863 (95 % CI, 0.795-0.931), lower for true- and false-lumen than for whole-aorta delineation. DL showed encouraging detection accuracy and higher sensitivity and specificity than the radiologist comparators in five head-to-head studies read under experimental conditions, supporting assistive triage rather than replacement; lumen-level segmentation remains more challenging than whole-aorta contouring. Certainty was low - datasets were predominantly case-control with a median prevalence of 50 %, heterogeneity was substantial and small-study effects pronounced - so these estimates are experimental upper bounds requiring prospective confirmation.

title: Three decades of Rex shunt for pediatric extrahepatic portal vein obstruction: A narrative review of advances from surgical evolution to holistic management.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Since its introduction in 1992, the Rex shunt (also called Meso-Rex bypass, MRB) has substantially advanced the management of pediatric extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO) by restoring physiological hepatopetal portal flow. However, a comprehensive synthesis of the accumulating evidence and evolving practices is notably lacking, especially given that the latest Baveno VI consensus was published nine years ago in 2016. OBJECTIVE: This review aims to synthesize three decades of advances in Rex shunt evolution, from a novel technique to a widely adopted first-line surgical option. METHODS: We conducted a narrative review, synthesizing evidence from key studies, large case series, and expert consensus statements. RESULTS: Key topics addressed include the comparison between Rex shunt and portosystemic shunts, evolving surgical indications, technical evolution of the procedure, critical aspects of perioperative management, identification of prognostic factors, and management of vascular complications. The review highlights the superior potential of the Rex shunt in resolving the sequelae of EHPVO and outlines the importance of a holistic management approach. CONCLUSION: The Rex shunt represents a major advance in the management of pediatric EHPVO. Optimal outcomes depend on careful patient selection, meticulous surgical technique, and comprehensive perioperative care, supported by an experienced multidisciplinary team.

title: Early outcomes after acute type A aortic dissection repair: Adequate perfusion, rather than cannulation strategy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal arterial cannulation strategy for acute type A aortic dissection repair remains uncertain. We aimed to evaluate the association between cannulation strategy and early postoperative outcomes and to identify perioperative factors associated with adverse events. METHODS: A single-center, retrospective cohort study was conducted at West China Hospital, Sichuan University, between January 2019 and June 2024, including consecutive patients undergoing repair of acute type A aortic dissection. Primary outcomes were in-hospital death and postoperative neurologic complications. Multivariable logistic regression and propensity-score matching were used to evaluate associations with early outcomes. RESULTS: Among 866 patients, femoral, axillary, and combined femoral + axillary cannulation were used in 694 (80.1%), 144 (16.6%), and 28 (3.2%) patients, respectively. Patients in the axillary and combined groups more frequently had primary arch tears and underwent more extensive arch repair. In-hospital death occurred in 43 (5.0%) patients and postoperative neurologic complications in 113 (13.0%) patients, with comparable rates across groups; paraplegia was more frequent in the combined group (2/28 [7.1%]; P = .03). In multivariable analysis, axillary cannulation was not independently associated with in-hospital death (odds ratio, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 0.69-4.03), postoperative neurologic complications (odds ratio, 0.73; 95% confidence interval, 0.37-1.34), or cerebral infarction (odds ratio, 1.05; 95% confidence interval, 0.51-2.01). Preoperative shock (odds ratio, 3.20; 95% confidence interval, 1.44-6.91) and higher peak intraoperative lactate (odds ratio, 1.22; 95% confidence interval, 1.14-1.30) were independently associated with in-hospital death. In 142 propensity score-matched femoral-axillary pairs, mortality and neurologic complication rates remained similar. CONCLUSION: Cannulation strategy was not independently associated with in-hospital death or postoperative neurologic complications. Preoperative shock and higher peak intraoperative lactate were more consistently associated with adverse early outcomes, supporting the clinical importance of timely systemic reperfusion and effective cerebral protection.

title: Prognostic Value of Psoas Muscle Index Improvement in Patients Undergoing Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt.
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the prognostic value of early psoas muscle index (PMI) improvement after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) placement in patients with cirrhosis and sarcopenia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: 2 2 2 2 This multicenter retrospective study included 390 patients with cirrhosis and sarcopenia who underwent TIPS at 5 tertiary centers between February 2016 and April 2023. PMI was measured on computed tomography (CT) before TIPS and ∼1 month afterward. Sarcopenia reversal was defined as a post-TIPS PMI above the sex-specific cutoff values (>6.36 cm/mfor men and >3.92 cm/mfor women). Associations of PMI improvement with overall survival and overt hepatic encephalopathy (OHE) were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses. Receiver-operating characteristic analysis identified optimal cutoff values. RESULTS: At 1 month after TIPS, 188 patients (48.2%) achieved sarcopenia reversal. Sarcopenia reversal was associated with higher cumulative survival (84.6% vs 68.2%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.24; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.14-0.41; P < .001) and lower OHE incidence (16.6% vs 51.1%; HR, 0.26; 95% CI, 0.17-0.39; P < .001). The PMI improvement rate was an independent predictor of mortality and OHE. Optimal cutoff values were 11.8% for mortality and 15.8% for OHE. Patients with PMI improvement above these thresholds had significantly better survival and lower OHE incidence (both P < .001). CONCLUSIONS: PMI improvement assessed at 1 month after TIPS is independently associated with reduced mortality and OHE in patients with cirrhosis and sarcopenia. PMI assessment 1 month after TIPS may provide a simple imaging biomarker for early prognostic evaluation and risk stratification.

title: Drug-Eluting Stents versus Drug-Coated Balloons Plus Bare-Metal Stents for the Treatment of Femoropopliteal Artery Lesions: 2-Year Outcomes from the TALENT Study.
abstract: PURPOSE: To compare the 2-year outcomes of drug-eluting stents (DES) versus drug-coated balloons (DCB) plus bare-metal stents (BMS) in patients with femoropopliteal artery disease. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Data were analyzed from The Impact of Tibial Runoff on Clinical Outcome of Endovascular Therapy in Femoropopliteal Lesions (TALENT) study, a multicenter, prospective study. Inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied to balance baseline characteristics. The primary outcomes were freedom of all-cause mortality, freedom of major adverse events, clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR), and major adverse limb events (MALEs), and the secondary outcomes were the improvement in Rutherford classification and changes in quality of life assessed by the 25-item Vascular Quality of Life questionnaire. RESULTS: A total of 429 patients were included (81 in DES group; 348 in DCB plus BMS group). During a median (Q1-Q3) follow-up of 20.2 months (11.6-27.1 months), no significant differences were observed between the 2 groups in 2-year freedom of all-cause mortality (91.4% vs 85.1%; P = .096), freedom of major adverse events (79.6% vs 73.9%; P = .330), CD-TLR (9.6% vs 12.6%; P = .737), and MALEs (10.1% vs 12.3%; P = .612). Both treatment modalities significantly improved in VascuQol score and Rutherford classification, with improvement rates of 76.1% and 71.3% at 24 months, respectively. An interaction effect (P = .014 and .005, respectively) was observed for patients with intermittent claudication (R2-R3), suggesting that DES may be associated with lower risks of CD-TLR and MALEs. CONCLUSIONS: Over the 2-year follow-up, DES and DCB plus BMS demonstrated favorable and comparable overall effectiveness in real-world patients with complex femoropopliteal lesions.

title: The Effect of Different Supervised Exercise Modalities on Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Supervised exercise is currently recognized as the first-line treatment for patients with peripheral artery disease. However, the comparative benefits of treadmill training, arm-ergometry, and leg-ergometry remain unclear. REVIEW METHODS: Medline, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to May 7, 2025, for randomized controlled trials in adults with peripheral artery disease. Eligible studies involved supervised treadmill, arm-ergometry, or leg-ergometry interventions lasting 12 to 24 weeks and compared these interventions with other exercise modalities or nonexercise controls. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was conducted to estimate mean differences (MDs) with 95% CI for peak oxygen uptake, maximal walking distance, and pain-free walking distance. SUMMARY: Eleven trials involving 519 participants were included. Arm-ergometry increased peak oxygen uptake by 1.85 mL/kg/min (95% CI, 0.99-2.71 mL/kg/min, P < .01), and treadmill training increased peak oxygen uptake by 1.46 mL/kg/min (95% CI, 1.12-1.81 mL/kg/min, P < .01) compared with control. Treadmill training increased maximal walking distance (MD = 191.25: 95% CI, 66.84-315.65 m, P < .01), whereas arm-ergometry showed no significant difference (MD = 121.35: 95% CI, -45.61 to 288.32 m, P = .15). In addition, pain-free walking distance improved with treadmill training (MD = 181.88: 95% CI, 154.99-208.76 m, P < .01), arm-ergometry (MD = 78.11: 95% CI, 54.62-101.60 m, P < .01), and leg-ergometry (MD = 51.08: 95% CI, 8.27-93.89 m, P = .02) compared with control.

title: MitraNav: Design and Modeling of a Robotic System for Transseptal Mitral Valve Replacement with Dock Catheter Task-Space Control.
abstract: PURPOSE: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is a promising therapy for reducing mitral regurgitation in select patients. Direct tip control of multi-segment catheters can simplify manipulation and enable precise, stable positioning. This paper introduces MitraNav, the first robotic system developed for dock-based TMVR, focusing on system design and task-space control of the dock catheter. METHODS: Built on a previously validated guide-sheath robot, MitraNav is upgraded to support concentric multi-catheter manipulation via a unified actuation mechanism. It suits both dock and balloon catheters, enabling all catheter manipulation using a single robotic system. A two-segment bending model maps joint space to task space through an intermediate configuration space. A two-stage control strategy is then applied: joint-space control allows for rapid approach to the mitral annulus, followed by task-space control for direct tip positioning. To improve accuracy and handle joint limits, the task-space controller incorporates Jacobian normalization to balance joint contributions, null-space optimization to regulate joint motion without affecting the primary task, and a PD controller to reduce tracking errors. RESULTS: Trajectory-following experiments demonstrate feasibility of direct tip control, with maximum errors of 2.38 mm, 2.53 mm, and 2.46 mm in three trials. These positional errors are within the range of acceptable accuracy commonly considered for catheter-based cardiac interventions. CONCLUSION: MitraNav represents the foundation for intuitive catheter manipulation and offers the potential for semi-autonomous robotic dock-based TMVR.

title: Influence of Hypertension on the Regional Elastic Properties of Ascending Thoracic Aortic Aneurysms with Bicuspid Aortic Valves.
abstract: Although hypertension may affect the local biomechanical properties of ascending thoracic aortic aneurysms (ATAAs) with a bicuspid aortic valve (BAV), a comparison of the regional elastic properties of BAV-ATAAs between patients with and without hypertension is not yet available due to lack of biomechanical data. In this study, we collected 25 fresh ATAA samples from 17 hypertensive and 8 age-matched non-hypertensive patients who underwent elective aortic surgery. Biomechanical tests were executed to investigate the regional failure stresses and biaxial mechanical properties of BAV-ATAAs with and without hypertension. A material model was fitted to the biaxial experimental data to obtain model parameters in different regions. Histological analysis was performed to investigate the underlying microstructure and determine the percentages of elastic and collagen fibers. The circumferential failure stresses in the anterior, lateral, and posterior regions were significantly lower for the hypertensive group than in the non-hypertensive group. Regarding equibiaxial stresses, the hypertensive BAV-ATAAs showed significantly higher longitudinal tissue stiffness in the anterior and lateral regions than the non-hypertensive BAV-ATAAs. Collagen fiber hyperplasia was observed in the anterior and lateral regions of both the hypertensive and non-hypertensive BAV-ATAAs. However, in these regions the laminar structure of the elastic fibers was disrupted in several places and apoptotic smooth muscle cells were observed in the group with hypertension compared to the group without hypertension. In addition, the circumferential failure stresses in the anterior and lateral regions were significantly increased in the hypertensive group and strongly correlated with the collagen content. These results suggest that the regional elastic properties of the hypertensive BAV-ATAAs are more deteriorated than those of the non-hypertensive samples. Due to the significant impact on circumferential tensile strength, the hypertensive BAV patients may be at a higher risk of ATAA rupture than non-hypertensive BAV patients.
